characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: flat dog-bone-shaped specimens, gage length 25 mm, length along RD
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, strain rate 10^-3 s^-1, three measurements averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine tensile properties (YS, UTS, TE, SYS, SUTS)

characterization_methods.key_findings: DP1000-1: GROD map almost entirely yellow (fully recrystallized austenite); thinner, more interrupted red δ ferrite bands with 'Annealing twins'; Rex-γ 91.6 %, α 9.1 %, δ 10.5 %, γ grain size 5.13 ± 4.74 µm.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: phase (PH) mappings and grain-reference-orientation-deviation (GROD) mappings of austenite; Rex-γ defined by GROD < 2°; high-angle boundaries > 15°
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify recrystallized austenite and α/δ ferrite fractions and assess recrystallization state

characterization_methods.key_findings: In the developed duplex steel κ-carbides and Cr7C3 carbides appear at 950–1000 °C and disappear at 1050 °C (Fig. 1a); the ferrite fraction by XRD for DP1000-1 is not reported in Table 1.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: phase constituents of the annealed CR structure measured after annealing at 600–1050 °C for 5 min (Fig. 1a); ferrite fraction determined from XRD (supplementary materials)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase constituents and determine ferrite fraction

defect_interactions.interaction_type: crack nucleation at α/γ interfaces and capture/deflection by δ ferrite bands
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Granular α ferrite grains can restrain austenite grain growth, but cracks are also easily initiated at the α/γ interfaces during deformation; these cracks can be captured and deflected by the δ ferrite bands, where they even get blunted.

interfaces.interface_notes: The Cr7C3 carbides and intergranular κ-carbides formed at 950 °C are significantly dissolved when the annealing temperature is raised to 1000 °C (the DP1000-1 condition).
interfaces.phase_evolution: At 950 °C austenite transforms to ferrite + Cr7C3 carbides + intergranular κ-carbides; ferrite-to-austenite transformation occurs above 950 °C; during annealing at 1000 °C the Cr7C3 carbides and intergranular κ-carbides dissolve significantly.

processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting and casting into ingot
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melted in a vacuum induction furnace under argon atmosphere and cast into ingot.
HR plates heated to 1050 °C, isothermally held 0.5 h, then quenched in water.
Cold rolled to 3 mm thickness (CR parent state of the DP specimens).
Defining annealing step for DP1000-1: the CR sheet was annealed at 1000 °C for 1 min and then water quenched.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Three tensile measurements were made for each heat treatment condition and the average values taken.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat dog-bone-shaped tensile specimens, gage length 25 mm, length direction along the rolling direction (RD)

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve of DP1000-1 shown in Fig. 3a (orange curve); it peaks highest among the long (>40 % TE) curves, near 30 % strain between the 1200 and 1350 MPa gridlines.

structures.microstructure_counts: 2 ferrite morphologies (granular α ferrite and banded δ ferrite) plus the austenite matrix

phases_present.morphology: recrystallized austenite matrix grains with annealing twins

microstructure_list.region: austenite grain boundaries and triple points

phases_present.morphology: band-like, elongated along RD; in DP1000-1 the bands are thinner and more interrupted than in DP950-5

microstructure_list.region: bands elongated along the rolling direction (RD)

structures.overall_structure: Austenite–ferrite duplex microstructure in the DP1000-1 condition (CR structure annealed at 1000 °C for 1 min + water quench): an almost fully recrystallized austenite matrix (Rex-γ = 91.6 %) together with two ferrite morphologies, i.e. granular α ferrite and banded δ ferrite; annealing twins present and the δ ferrite bands are thinner and more interrupted than in the 950 °C specimens.

unmapped_findings: Specific yield strength (SYS) of DP1000-1 is 169.0 ± 1.6 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ and specific ultimate tensile strength (SUTS) is 203.6 ± 2.4 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ (b0019 Table 1); these specific-strength metrics have no dedicated slot in the property schema.

The DP1000-1 γ grain size (5.13 ± 4.74 µm) is the smallest among the fully recrystallized conditions and grows to 7.40 ± 5.13 µm in DP1000-5 and 9.65 ± 8.17 µm in DP1050-1 as annealing temperature/period increase, because the number and fraction of granular α ferrite (which retards austenite grain growth) decrease (b0024).
The alloy has an ultralow density of 6.36 g·cm⁻³ measured by buoyancy balance according to Archimedes Principle (b0009, b0012); this alloy-level value underlies the specific strength of DP1000-1.

Equilibrium phase fractions were calculated (Thermo-Calc type Calphad) over 550–1400 °C (Fig. S1): the calculated ferrite fraction is almost constant at about 33 % between 991 °C and 1250 °C and increases to a maximum as the temperature decreases from 991 °C to 854 °C, whereas the largest measured ferrite fraction by XRD occurs at 900 °C (b0015). This calculation is alloy/heat-treatment level rather than DP1000-1-specific.
The abstract headline values (UTS 1250 MPa and TE 41.4 % at density 6.36 g·cm⁻³) belong to DP1000-5, not to DP1000-1 (DP1000-1: UTS 1295 ± 15 MPa, TE 27.4 ± 0.7 %) (b0009, b0019).

Fig. 3a places the DP1000-1 engineering stress–strain curve as the highest-peaking curve among the long-ductility (>40 % TE) conditions, terminating near 30 % strain (figure_003); the exact curve coordinates are not tabulated.

Fig. 3b plots DP1000-1 as a red star in the SUTS–TE comparison map with 2000-series Al alloys, Ti6Al4V, austenitic and duplex steels; however, the text's explicit comparative statement (SUTS×TE product exceeding 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·%) is made only for DP1000-5 and DP1050-1, not for DP1000-1 (b0026, figure_003).
Nanoindentation (Fig. S4) showed ferrite is clearly softer than Rexed austenite; this result is presented for DP1000-5, not specifically for DP1000-1 (b0025).
